issues.legal_issue: Section 5 of the Limitation Act does not permit condonation of delay in an application to enforce a statutory right of pre-emption when the special law prescribes a filing period but provides no extension mechanism for that application.
material_facts: In both appeals, applicants sought pre-emption under a land-reform statute as adjoining or contiguous landowners.
The statute prescribed a specific period for making a pre-emption application, but did not provide for extending that period or applying the principles of Section 5 to such applications.
The same statute expressly provided for extension or application of Section 5 in relation to certain appeals and revisions, but contained no corresponding provision for pre-emption applications.
The applications were filed years after the transfers, beyond the applicable statutory period; one applicant relied on lack of knowledge of the transfer and sought condonation.
issues.conclusion: Section 5 of the Limitation Act is unavailable to condone delay in an application under the special law for pre-emption. The specific period prescribed by that law governs, and a late application must be dismissed; Article 137 does not supply a different period.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 3, 5 and 29(2) of the Limitation Act, Section 5 may apply to a period prescribed by special or local law unless its application is expressly excluded. Applying Hukumdev Narain Yadav v. Lalit Narain Mishra and Anwari Basavaraj Patil v. Siddaramaiah, exclusion may be gathered from the scheme and nature of the special law, even without express words. The court relied also on Commissioner of Sales Tax v. Parson Tools and Plants and approved Serish Maji v. Nishit Kumar Dolui. It treated an application under Section 8 of the West Bengal Land Reforms Act as in the nature of a suit for limitation purposes, noting the references to pre-emption suits in Section 8 and Article 97 of the Limitation Act; Article 137 therefore did not govern. The express provision for applying Section 5 to other proceedings under the special law, coupled with its omission for pre-emption applications and the statute's specific filing period, showed exclusion. The court distinguished Mangu Ram v. Municipal Corporation of Delhi and Mukri Gopalan v. Cheppilat Puthanpurayil Aboobacker, and referred to Mattoo Devi v. Damodar Lal for the weak nature of the pre-emption right and the need to exercise it strictly.

predicates.preemption_application_under_self_contai: A person applied under a special law to enforce a statutory right of pre-emption.
predicates.special_law_sets_filing_period: The special law prescribed a period for making the pre-emption application.
predicates.special_law_allows_extension_for_other_p: The special law provided for extending time or applying sufficient-cause principles to some other proceedings, but made no such provision for pre-emption applications.
predicates.application_filed_after_filing_period: The pre-emption application was made after the filing period prescribed by the special law had expired.

issues.definition: When a pre-emption application under a special law is late, and that law sets a filing period while allowing extensions for other proceedings but not for pre-emption applications, the application cannot be condoned.
